name: Saar Protectorate (1947–1956)
description: A white Nordic cross on a field whose hoist quarters are blue and fly quarters red.
history: The flag of the Saar Protectorate, the French-controlled Saarland separated from Germany after the Second World War, was laid down in the constitution of 17 December 1947 and by law of 16 June 1948; its blue, white and red are the French colours. Nicknamed the 'Saarlappen', it was abolished when the Saar joined the Federal Republic on 1 January 1957.

features.symbolism: a Scandinavian cross chosen for the Saar's aspirations to European union
